title: Covid-19 Cases Rise in Kolkata During Monsoon as Doctors Urge Vigilance
excerpt: At least four patients are being treated at private hospitals in the city, with doctors saying the virus now behaves like seasonal flu and poses serious risk mainly to the elderly and immunocompromised.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Kolkata has four Covid-19 patients in private hospitals, including a child and two elderly in ICU.
  • Current infections resemble the Omicron wave, with mild symptoms like cough and fever.
  • Health officials advise vulnerable groups to take precautions during the monsoon season.
  • Covid-19 cases are rising in Andhra Pradesh and Pune, but no new booster recommendations issued.

Kolkata is reporting a gradual uptick in Covid-19 hospitalizations alongside a broader wave of seasonal respiratory infections driven by the monsoon, prompting doctors to call for measured vigilance rather than alarm.

At least four patients have been admitted to private hospitals across the city. A 10-year-old boy from the Garia area in southern Kolkata was admitted on July 18 after developing fever, cough, and shortness of breath. His swab test returned positive, and he was transferred to ICU isolation, according to NDTV. Three additional patients are being treated at Fortis Hospital.

"We are treating three patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. One has recovered and is being discharged, while two required ICU admission due to low oxygen levels but have responded well to treatment and are now stable."

— Dr. Subhajit Sen, Consultant Pulmonologist and Critical Care Specialist, Fortis Hospital, Kolkata

Endemic Phase, Not a New Wave

Health officials and doctors across Kolkata have moved to calm fears, emphasizing that SARS-CoV-2 has transitioned into an endemic state, behaving much like seasonal influenza. The current infections closely mirror the Omicron wave pattern, with most patients experiencing mild upper respiratory symptoms — fever, sore throat, cough, and body aches.

Dr. Judhajit Sengupta, consultant in critical care medicine at Narayana RN Tagore Hospital in Mukundapur, told the Telegraph India that "Covid-19 has largely become like a common seasonal flu." He noted that many people with mild symptoms are no longer opting for testing.

> **"Three additional patients are being treated at Fortis Hospital.

"We are treating three patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection."**

The Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium (INSACOG) continues to monitor circulating strains, which are primarily sub-variants of the Omicron lineage. Current evidence suggests these variants do not cause more severe illness or spread significantly faster than earlier Omicron strains, according to NDTV.

![Fortis Hospital. Three additional patients are being treated at Fortis Hospital.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/8a/Fortis_Hospital_Noida_-_panoramio.jpg)

Monsoon Fuels Respiratory Infections

The uptick in Covid-19 cases comes alongside a broader rise in influenza, adenoviruses, rhinoviruses, and mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue and malaria — all typical of India's monsoon season. Dr. Debadeep Dutta, a Kolkata-based general physician, told the Telegraph India that respiratory infections and vector-borne diseases "typically increase during this season."

At Techno India DAMA Hospital, Medical Superintendent Dr. M.S. Purkait said that while no admitted patient has been confirmed Covid-positive, two patients with lower respiratory tract infections are showing symptoms consistent with mild Covid-19 and are being closely monitored.

Who Is Most at Risk

While most infections are mild and manageable at home, doctors flagged specific groups that remain vulnerable to severe complications: older adults, pregnant women, children, people with asthma, COPD, chronic liver disease, diabetes, or weakened immunity.

"The focus should be on protecting those at higher risk of complications, including the elderly and those with underlying medical conditions or compromised immunity."

— Apoorbaa Roy, Consultant Microbiologist, Neuberg Pulse Diagnostics
Vulnerable Groups During Monsoon
›Elderly individuals are at higher risk.

Dr. Dutta specifically advised people above 60, along with those on long-term steroids or managing tuberculosis, to seek medical attention if fever persists beyond a week, breathlessness develops, or oxygen levels fall.

Cases Rising Beyond Kolkata

The trend extends beyond West Bengal. Andhra Pradesh reported 12 Covid-19 infections between June 26 and July 16, with four deaths among patients with comorbidities. Pune is also seeing new cases after nearly three years of relative quiet, according to NDTV.

Despite the uptick, the Indian government has not issued any recommendation for an additional booster dose. Doctors continue to recommend annual influenza vaccination for high-risk groups and stress that existing treatment protocols — home isolation for mild cases, oxygen support and antivirals for severe illness — remain effective.

What Comes Next

Health officials say they are maintaining close surveillance but have not detected an unusual surge. Periodic, localized upticks are expected for an endemic virus, particularly during monsoon season. Hospitals remain prepared with established protocols.

For the Indian diaspora with family in Kolkata and other affected cities, doctors advise encouraging elderly relatives to wear masks in crowded indoor spaces, maintain hand hygiene, avoid unnecessary gatherings, and consult a physician promptly if symptoms worsen — especially those with chronic conditions.

"Vigilance, not fear, is the need of the hour," said Dr. Sen.
